independentPageFindings.finding: Three-stage game enforces current observation secrecy until prediction, unit feasibility, and squared loss. IID fixed distribution, mean/variance benchmark, equations1.1/1.2 and success are expected quantities. Their asserted optimality/nonnegativity is not the deterministic empirical-best lower bound.

Expected-fixed minimum is outside expectation. Deterministic hindsight minimum and general fixed-u regret are separately defined. The no-regret text visibly prints ordinary lim, not limsup, and permits a nonpositive value. Footnote alternate prediction set, dynamic-comparator reference and suppressed-loss remark are accounted for.

The pathwise argument allows data chosen after the prediction. The hindsight mean assertion lacks its square-completion proof. FTL uses strictly earlier outcomes, with any initial unit value informally; this is not an IID premise.

All BTL induction/cancellation/minimizer/feasibility steps were checked. Theorem1.3 specifically chooses 1/2 initially and a positive finite horizon; it states only the upper bound4+4lnT. Minimax lower bound remains explicitly unproved.
Checked replacement by final mean, BTL subtraction direction, first-round1/4, difference-of-squares factor, mean-shift algebra, loose4/t bound, final harmonic sum and figure role.

Checked shifted reciprocal integral and logarithm endpoint; proof-summary upper conclusion does not prove every fixed-comparator ordinary limit. Parameter/computation remarks and all historical citations are explicitly excluded with reasons, not mistaken for proof dependencies.

routeAudit.review: Feasible mean requires unit bounds; optimality follows the omitted square-completion bridge. The assertion is correctly not treated as an already printed proof.
Cancellation leaves the prefix inequality. IH compares to the old minimizer; minimizer property compares that fixed old minimizer to the feasible final minimizer. Transitivity direction is correct.
T=1 is reflexivity. The local IH is discharged by induction, not introduced as a public hypothesis or circular theorem premise.
BTL gives sum current-leader losses <= final-best loss. Subtracting reverses this comparison into the desired regret upper bound; all prefix minimizers are supplied by the mean characterization.
Initial-half is a theorem premise explicitly cited in premise_discharge, not inferred from generic game rules. x*_1=y_1 makes the current-best loss zero and the first gap <=1/4.
Both neighboring positive-prefix means and y_t lie in [0,1]; the factor |x*_{t-1}+x*_t-2y_t| is <=2.
At t>=2 both denominators are nonzero. Splitting the current sum gives the displayed adjacent-mean difference.
Triangle inequality and bounds on the prefix sum and new observation imply the printed loose bound 4/t. A possible sharper bound must not replace the source constant silently.
First-round 1/4 and t>=2 bounds sum to the displayed expression, then relax to 4 times the harmonic sum.
For integer t>=2, 1/t <= integral_t^{t+1} 1/(s-1) ds. Add the first term 1 and evaluate at T+1 and 2; T=1 has an empty integral. Figure is illustrative, not a necessary premise.
Combining harmonic and preceding regret bounds gives 4+4 log T at positive horizons.
Theorem scope retains arbitrary unit-bounded finite outcomes and initial half. The informal earlier arbitrary first prediction does not erase this specialization.
The paragraph summarizes an upper-bound route. An ordinary zero quotient additionally needs a lower bound; no fixed-u existence edge is created.
Equation1.2 is equation1.1 divided by positive T. The stochastic criterion and its unproved risk/normalization bridges stay distinct from deterministic five-target claims.
The variance update telescopes with the actual initial-half loss. Reviewed as derived algebra only, with nonnegative identity valid even for unrestricted real data.
One sufficient route: derived lower bound plus printed upper bound and analytic normalization.
Alternative sufficient route: exact identity plus unit bounds and harmonic estimate. It does not additionally require the printed BTL route.
Subtract completed-square fixed loss. All-real u is allowed algebraically, but it is a generalization of the feasible source comparator domain.
Only a one-sided eventual upper bound follows. No ordinary-limit existence is discharged here.
Both directions use best-average convergence and eventual positive-T identity. Extra squared-distance/mean convergence is explicitly conditional, not a hidden source premise.
Factorial endpoint blocks give two distinct quotient limits. This is a separately checked diagnostic, not an implementation dependency or a silent source correction.
